correctness.rationale: Decodability from a binary linear encoder rowspace R at receiver i is equivalent by finite-dimensional duality to existence in R of an index-i-one vector supported in {i-1,i,i+1}; this is exact for the stated five-receiver C5 scalar unicast instance. Independently enumerated ALL 1,31,155,155,31,1 subspaces of F2^5 by dimension 0..5 and applied this criterion. Valid counts by dimension are 0,0,0,20,16,1, proving scalar minimum length3 and exactly20 row-space classes. Full D10 action on the twenty yields four size-five orbits with stabilizer2; each has a distinct Hamming weight enumerator. |GL(3,2)|=168 bases per rowspace, so precisely3360 full-rank 3x5 matrices. Submitted second 4^5 fitting-matrix census and source representative bases were inspected; independent subspace/D10 calculation verified the key counts without trusting logs. This is an exact finite proof, not a partial search.

value.rationale: The pentagon is the canonical smallest odd-hole index-coding instance, where minimum codelength alone is classical. Full equality-layer classification of binary scalar optimizers is a natural finite extremal problem: 20 distinct output-basis classes and 4 dihedral orbits with different weight enumerators distinguish genuine codes rather than arbitrary matrix presentations. This is motivated independently of claiming a better broadcast rate.

limitations: Classification is of five-message binary scalar unicast C5 only; optimal length3 already classical.
